title: Hourly bull flag: steep 6-hour pole, tight low-volume pause, buy the break above the pole high

source.title: Flags, Bulkowski's Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns site (thepatternsite.com)

rule_summary: Chart 1h, closed bars only; signal at the close of bar t, fill at the open of t+1. At bar t, search for a pole top p with t-9 <= p <= t-3 such that high(p) is the highest high of bars p..t-1. POLE: PL = lowest low of bars p-5..p; require high(p)/PL - 1 >= 0.025 (a rise of at least 2.5% within 6 bars) and H = high(p) - PL. FLAG = bars p+1..t-1 (2 to 8 bars). Conditions: (1) depth: lowest low of the flag FL >= high(p) - 0.5*H (retrace at most half the pole); (2) tightness: (highest high - lowest low of the flag) <= 0.5*H; (3) volume dries up: mean volume of the flag bars <= 0.7 * mean volume of bars p-5..p; (4) close(t) > SMA(168) of 1h closes. If several p qualify, use the most recent. ENTRY at the close of t when close(t) > high(p) AND no open position AND that pole has not already been traded. STOP at FL, fixed at entry. TARGET (measured move) FL + H, a limit exit. TIME EXIT at the close of the 24th bar after the entry bar (filled next open). No pyramiding, no other filters.
mechanism: Bulkowski gives the shape (steep pole, short tight flag, volume trending down during the flag, measured move equal to the pole added to the flag low) but no causal reason. The closest honest one: the pole is a burst of new demand (news or a large buyer); the flag is short-term holders taking profit, absorbed without much price give-back on shrinking volume, which shows that supply is thin; a close back above the pole high triggers breakout buyers and stops of those who sold the pause, so the original flow resumes. The other side are profit-takers and faders who sell too early. Requiring a pole of at least 2.5% and a target equal to the pole height means the planned gain is roughly 2.5% or more per trade against a 0.30-0.45% round trip, with the stop at the flag low.
